lemma: Cut lemma. Let C be a Boolean circuit (fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT) on inputs x_1..x_n, and let (A,B) be a partition of the input variables. Let the gates be split into sides S_A and S_B (each gate on the side it is assigned), and let kappa be the number of wires (gate-input edges, including input-variable edges) whose endpoints lie on different sides. Let M be the 2^|A| x 2^|B| communication matrix of f = C, with rows indexed by a in {0,1}^A and columns by b in {0,1}^B. Then log2 rank_R(M) <= kappa + 1.
gap: Open: the aggregated bound over many partitions. A single partition gives log2 rank <= kappa(P)+1; summing kappa over a family of partitions counts a gate once for every partition it crosses, so sum_P kappa(P) is not bounded by |C| in general (reuse). Need an account that bounds the cumulative cost, or a counterexample showing the aggregate exceeds polylog(N)*|C|.

proved_step: PROOF. Each cross wire carries one bit from its source side to its target side. Evaluate C in topological order: a gate on side S_A needs only values from S_A or from cross wires; the value of a cross wire is a function of its source side's inputs and bits already received, so it is sent once, by its source party, as one bit. Each cross wire contributes at most one bit, so the transcript has at most kappa bits. Once all cross wires are transmitted, both parties know the output bit for their input pair; the party holding the output gate sends one more bit, so the total is at most kappa+1 bits. A deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; each leaf is a combinatorial rectangle on which the output is constant, so M is a sum of at most 2^c rank-one 0/1 matrices, rank_R(M) <= 2^c. Hence log2 rank <= kappa+1. The argument uses only the wire count, not any gate structure, and it holds for any partition of gates. Remark: the lab check uses the 0-based side assignment and counts each gate input once, matching the wire count above.

proved_step: L-K1-PREFIX (closes G0005(a) for the prefix-cut family). Setting: f:{0,1}^N->{0,1} computed by a fan-in<=2 circuit C with gates G, inputs x_1..x_N in a fixed order. Define P(x_j)=j and P(g)=max of P over the inputs of gate g (so P(u)<=P(g) along every wire u->g, and 1<=P(v)<=N). Let W = number of wires (gate-input edges), Lambda(C)=sum over wires u->g of (P(g)-P(u)). For i in [1,N-1], M_i = communication matrix of f for A={x_1..x_i}, B=rest. CLAIM: (1) sum_{i=1}^{N-1} log2 rank_R(M_i) <= (N-1) + Lambda(C); (2) Lambda(C) <= W(N-1) <= 2|G|(N-1); hence for every input order, |G| >= (sum_i log2 rank_R(M_i) - (N-1)) / (2(N-1)). PROOF. Let L_i={v: P(v)<=i}. Input x_j is in L_i iff j<=i, so L_i restricted to inputs is exactly A. If g in L_i and u->g is a wire, P(u)<=P(g)<=i so u in L_i: no wire goes from the right side to the left side. Hence the cross wires for cut i are exactly the wires with P(u)<=i<P(g); call their number kappa_i. This is a legal gate split for (A,B), so S0001 (SURVIVED_REVIEW) gives log2 rank_R(M_i) <= kappa_i+1. Summing over i: sum_i kappa_i = sum over wires of #{i in [1,N-1]: P(u)<=i<P(g)} = sum over wires of (P(g)-P(u)), because 1<=P(u) and P(g)<=N. So the sum is <= Lambda(C)+(N-1). (2) holds since 0<=P(g)-P(u)<=N-1 and each gate has at most 2 wires. Corollary (CEILING): rank_R(M_i) <= 2^{min(i,N-i)}, so sum_i log2 rank <= N^2/4 and the bound gives |G| >= (N^2/4-(N-1))/(2(N-1)) = N/8 - O(1) at most. The method cannot give a superlinear bound for any N-input function using prefix cuts.

proved_step: S0002 (repair of S0001, kind LEMMA). Setting: Boolean circuit C of fan-in at most 2 over AND, OR, NOT, with input nodes x_1..x_(n+m); Alice holds x_1..x_n, Bob holds the rest; f(a,b) is the output. Assign every node (inputs and gates) to a party. Let kappa = number of DAG edges whose endpoints lie on different parties, input edges included. For every node that has at least one crossing out-edge, its owner sends its value once; the number of such sources is at most kappa. The output owner sends the output bit (at most 1 more). The protocol is deterministic, costs at most kappa+1 and computes f. A protocol of cost c has at most 2^c leaves, each a combinatorial rectangle on which f is constant, so M_f is a sum of at most 2^c indicator rectangles over the 1-leaves and rank_Q M_f <= 2^c. This is an upper bound, not a lower bound, so the barrier check does not apply. Gap: the aggregate G0001 (cut costs over many partitions) stays open. refuted_approach: Route G0005(b) as stated (min over orders of the cone-span Lambda is O(|C| polylog N) for all circuits). Reason, to be checked by a different session: Lambda_pi is the total edge length of the circuit DAG under the linear order pi (a linear arrangement cost). For bounded-degree expander DAGs on n vertices the minimum linear arrangement cost is Omega(n^2), by the edge-expansion bound on every prefix cut. So min over orders of Lambda is not O(|C| polylog N) in general. This kills the Lambda bound as a route to G0001. It does not kill G0001: sum of log2 rank over prefix cuts is a different quantity from Lambda, and the upper bound log2 rank <= kappa+1 may be loose on such circuits. proved_step: LEMMA (subclass, cut width). Fix a variable order pi and a level l. Call a node prefix-side if its support lies in the first l variables. Let kappa_l be the number of prefix-side nodes with an edge into a non-prefix-side gate. Then the level width K_l (number of distinct residual functions C restricted to rho, for rho in {0,1}^l) satisfies K_l <= 2^kappa_l, because each non-prefix-side gate's value under rho depends on rho only through the constant values of the kappa_l crossing nodes. Hence the OBDD size for order pi is at most sum_l 2^kappa_l. COROLLARY: if kappa_l <= c log n for all l, then #SAT of C runs in poly(n, m) time by building the OBDD. This is the standard cut-width / OBDD-width technique and is not new; it is recorded only as a verified subclass.

lemma: Repaired cut width (single order, single level l). P = first l variables in order pi. X = prefix-side nodes feeding a gate whose support is not inside P, k = |X|. o = 1 if the output support is inside P, else 0. Then K_l <= 2^k if o = 0, and K_l <= 2 if o = 1. lemma: Single-order residual-width sum (identity order). C is a fan-in-2 circuit over x_0..x_{n-1} with gates G, output node out, computing f. For a node v let t(v) = bit_length of its support bitmask, so t(v) = 1 + max variable index in the support. Let Lambda(C) = sum over wires u->g of max(0, t(g) - t(u)). For l = 0..n let K_l = number of distinct residual functions f restricted to x_{<l} = rho, over rho in {0,1}^l. Then sum_{l=0}^{n} log2 K_l <= Lambda(C) + #{l : t(out) <= l}. Proof: fix l and P = {0..l-1}. Let X_l be the set of prefix-side nodes (support inside P) that feed a non-prefix gate. By the S0026 argument, if out is non-prefix then K_l <= 2^{|X_l|}; if out is prefix-side then K_l <= 2. Since supports grow along wires, t(g) >= t(u) for every wire u->g. Each w in X_l has a wire w->g with t(w) <= l < t(g), so |X_l| <= #{wires u->g : t(u) <= l < t(g)}. Summing over l, each wire with t(u) < t(g) is counted exactly t(g)-t(u) times, so sum_l |X_l| <= Lambda(C). Adding the at most one bit per level where out is prefix-side gives the claim. Scope: a single fixed variable order; Lambda depends on the order and can be about |C| * N for a bad order.

proved_step: REPAIR of S0001 (single-split cut lemma, input wires counted). Statement: Let C be a fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit on inputs X disjoint-union Y computing f, with communication matrix M_f (rows indexed by assignments to X, columns by assignments to Y). Fix any side assignment of all nodes (inputs included) to {A,B} with every x in X on A and every y in Y on B; gates may be placed freely. Let kappa = number of EDGES (u,g) of C with side(u) != side(g), input nodes included. Then rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). PROOF: fix a topological order v_1..v_T (inputs first). Alice holds a, Bob holds b. Process v_1..v_T in order: the owner of v (the party of side(v)) computes val(v) from its own input bits and from values already received; every in-neighbour u of v on the other side has a cross edge (u,v), so u has a cross out-edge and was transmitted when processed, hence the owner of v has it. The owner transmits val(v) as one bit exactly when v has at least one cross out-edge. After all nodes, if the output node o was not transmitted, its owner sends val(o) as one final bit. Both parties then know f(a,b). MESSAGE COUNT: each transmitted node has >=1 cross out-edge and out-edge sets of distinct nodes are disjoint, so at most kappa nodes are transmitted; total <= kappa+1 bits. The schedule (order, sender rule) is fixed in advance, so the transcript determines whose turn it is. RECTANGLE: a deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; the inputs reaching a leaf form a rectangle A_l x B_l (standard, since each message depends only on the sender's input and the transcript); f is constant on each leaf because val(o) is in the transcript (either transmitted or the final bit). So M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of 1_{A_l} 1_{B_l}^T, a sum of at most 2^(kappa+1) rank-one matrices, hence rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. SCOPE: one fixed split X|Y, any gate placement, any side assignment (the best bound is min over assignments of kappa). This is the standard circuit-to-communication argument (folklore, not claimed as new); it is bookkeeping, it does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (aggregate over many partitions) or G0005(a). It is not a LOWER_BOUND and does not trigger the barrier check. Consistency check on the refuted case: for IP_2 with all gates on Alice's side the input edges b1->AND1 and b2->AND2 are cross edges, so kappa=2 and the bound 8 >= rank 3; the gate-only count gives kappa=0 and the false bound 2.

proved_step: MINLA LEMMA (limit of the single-order prefix route; does not close G0001/G0002). Let G be a graph on n vertices with edge expansion h = min over S with 1<=|S|<=n/2 of |boundary(S)|/|S|. For any linear order v_1..v_n let cut_k = number of edges with one endpoint in {v_1..v_k} and the other outside. Then sum_{k=1}^{n-1} cut_k >= h*floor(n^2/4). PROOF: for k <= n/2, S={v_1..v_k} has |S| = k <= n/2, so cut_k >= h*k. For k > n/2, T={v_{k+1}..v_n} has |T| = n-k < n/2 and cut_k = |boundary(T)| >= h*(n-k). So cut_k >= h*min(k, n-k). Summing, and using sum_{k=1}^{n-1} min(k, n-k) = floor(n^2/4) (checked: n=3 gives 2, n=4 gives 4), the claim follows. CONSEQUENCE: for a fan-in-2 circuit C of size s whose underlying graph (all nodes, inputs included, n <= s + #inputs) has constant expansion h, the telescoping sum Lambda_pi = sum_k cut_k of the prefix chain (the identity sum_l kappa_l = Lambda_pi from the prefix cut lemma) is at least h*floor(n^2/4) = Omega(s^2) for EVERY order pi. So min over orders of Lambda_pi, and with it the bound sum_l log2 K_l <= Lambda_pi + n, is Omega(s^2) for such circuits and cannot give O(s polylog s). SCOPE: the lower bound is for any graph; it applies to any circuit family whose underlying graph is an expander, provided the expansion is verified for that family. lemma: REPAIR of the prefix-cut route (refuted by S0046 on expander-like circuits). Setup: C is a fan-in<=2 circuit with nodes = inputs x_1..x_n and gates, edges = wires u->g, output o. For a prefix length l, let P be a set of nodes that is closed under predecessors (g in P and u->g a wire imply u in P) and whose inputs are exactly x_1..x_l. Let w(P) = number of wires u->g with u in P and g not in P. Claim: the number of distinct subfunctions f(a,.), a in {0,1}^l, is at most 2^(w(P)). Hence the OBDD for the order x_1..x_n has size at most sum_l 2^(w_l), where w_l is the boundary of a closed prefix set at level l.
gap: NOT progress. (a) The bound is folklore (Wegener, BDD size versus cut-width); I do not claim novelty. (b) It is not an aggregate over partitions, so it does not close or shrink G0001 or G0002. (c) Closure under predecessors is stronger than the cut lemma S0044, which allows two-way communication. (d) Expander-like circuits have w_l >= h min(l, n-l) for every closed or non-closed set, so the bound is 2^(Omega(n)) on those families, consistent with S0046. The repair works only for bounded cut-width classes. Hand-checked only; no computation.
evidence: Hand proof by R1295 (session pnp-desk/research/R1295). No lab run was used for this step.
proved_step: PROOF. (1) By induction over a topological order, every node in P has a value that depends only on a, since P is closed under predecessors. (2) Let W be the set of wires leaving P; |W| = w(P). For any node outside P, its value is a function of its own inputs, which are either suffix inputs, outside gates, or wires in W. So for each suffix assignment b there is a function G_b with f(a,b) = G_b(z(a)), where z(a) in {0,1}^W lists the values carried by the wires in W. (3) Therefore f(a,.) = G_(.)(z(a)) is determined by z(a), which takes at most 2^(w(P)) values, so at most 2^(w(P)) distinct subfunctions occur. QED. Consequence: if every level l admits a closed prefix set with w_l <= W, then the OBDD has size at most n 2^W and #SAT of C takes time about n 2^W poly(s). For W = O(log s) this is polynomial.

proved_step: PROOF OF L1. (i) By induction on topological order, every A-node is a function of x alone: x-inputs trivially; an A-gate's inputs are A-nodes because no B-node feeds an A-gate. (ii) Let S(x) in {0,1}^kappa be the values of the kappa cross nodes (A-nodes with a B-consumer), which are functions of x by (i). By induction every B-node is a function of (y, S(x)): its inputs are y-inputs, B-nodes, or A-nodes, and any A-node feeding a B-node is a cross node, hence a coordinate of S(x). So f(x,y) = G(S(x), y) for some G. If the output node is an A-node, then f = h(x) and M_f has rank <= 1 <= 2^kappa. (iii) For s in {0,1}^kappa let u_s be the indicator vector of {x : S(x) = s} and w_s(y) = G(s,y). Then M_f = sum over s of u_s w_s^T, a sum of at most 2^kappa rank-<=1 matrices over Q, so rank_Q M_f <= 2^kappa. QED.

proved_step: PROOF OF L2. Fix a topological order v_1,...,v_N of the circuit. Let c_1,...,c_kappa be the nodes of K in that order; each c_i is owned by Alice (A) or Bob (B). Protocol: for i = 1..kappa the owner of c_i sends the bit value(c_i), then the output owner sends f's bit if f is not in K, i.e. at most kappa+1 bits. Well-defined and deterministic: the speaker sequence depends only on the circuit and the side assignment, not on the inputs. Correctness: when the owner of c_i speaks, it knows its own input and all bits sent so far, and it can compute c_i. Induction on the topological order: any input of c_i is either an input node (owned by the speaker, since inputs lie on their own side), a node on the speaker's side (computed by the speaker by induction), or a node on the other side with a consumer on the speaker's side, hence in K, hence earlier in the order and already sent. So value(c_i) is a function of the speaker's input and the transcript so far. Thus the transcript determines all of K and f. Rectangles: for a fixed transcript tau, the set of x with tau consistent is a set X_tau, and similarly Y_tau for y; by the standard induction over rounds the set {(x,y): transcript = tau} equals X_tau x Y_tau. On a leaf f is constant (it is determined by tau). Hence M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of u_tau w_tau^T with u, w 0/1 vectors, so rank_Q M_f <= number of leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

proved_step: Proof: Alice and Bob process gates in topological order. Each cross edge carries one bit, sent by the side that owns its source once the source value is determined from that side's inputs and previously received bits. Total communication is at most kappa bits. The output bit adds 1, so the deterministic communication complexity satisfies D(f) <= kappa+1. A deterministic protocol of depth d partitions the matrix into at most 2^d monochromatic rectangles, each of rank at most 1, so rank_R M_f <= 2^d. Hence log2 rank_R M_f <= kappa+1.

proved_step: Proof: Protocol: each cross edge carries the value of its source gate, sent by the owner of the source once that value is determined. Each gate is evaluated by the side that owns it, using its own inputs and bits received so far. Total communication is exactly kappa bits, so the protocol tree has at most 2^kappa leaves. For each leaf, the set of (a,b) reaching it is a combinatorial rectangle R_l on which f is constant. M_f = sum over 1-leaves of the indicator matrices of R_l. Each indicator of a rectangle has real rank at most 1, so rank_R(M_f) <= number of 1-leaves <= 2^kappa. Hence log2 rank_R(M_f) <= kappa.
